### PR 1 — head `claude/issue-19739-fleet-write-channel-text` → base `main`, draft

Title: `docs(pm): rest-channel names the fleet-write relay as the channel to the App identity`

Body:

Part of #19739

Clause-②: no

## What changed

One file, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/rest-channel.md`, section 〈通道边界〉: one paragraph of nine rule lines stating how the App identity is reached.

- `objectstack-fleet[bot]` is reached through the `fleet-write` relay; the four write tools (`post-stamped`, `label-write`, `issue-create`, `close-cards`) and `with-fleet.sh --via auto` share one selector.
- `dispatch` only when three conditions hold — `CCR_AGENT_PROXY_ENABLED=1`, a session id, a live relay — otherwise `direct`, with one printed line.
- The session id is derived from the container's `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`; `OS_FLEET_SESSION` overrides it for local checkouts and tests only.
- ⛔ Never prefix a command with it: the allow rules are literal prefixes, a prefixed write drops onto the classifier and the seat stalls.
- Live = the workflow file on `main` AND its Actions state `active`; the maintainer disabling it in the Actions UI turns the whole fleet back to `direct`.
- The dispatch goes to objectstack with the session token; the run executes on the runner with a per-run App token narrowed to the target repo.
- The closed op list lives in `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs`; reads stay direct.
- A `post-stamped` body over 60,000 bytes takes `direct` for that one write, with one printed line, as the seat's own user.
- A failed run (`post-stamped`/`close-cards` 4, `label-write`/`issue-create` 5) and UNCONFIRMED (6) are read, ⛔ never retried.

Spellings are taken from the #19755 branch `claude/issue-19755-fleet-write-derive-session` at 6470e4e (PR #19760): `sessionSource` in `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs`, `CONTAINER_SESSION_ENV` in `ops.mjs`, `relayLive`'s Actions-state read, the `with-fleet.sh --via auto` paragraph, and `sizeRoute` / `MAX_BODY_BYTES` in `post-stamped.mjs`. Everything else is read from `main` at 544767d (`.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml`: `repositories:` = the validated target, `permission-issues: write`, `permission-pull-requests: write`, `permission-metadata: read`).

**One correction to the card's item 3 wording.** The failed-run exit is not `4` fleet-wide. Each tool books it in its own register on that branch: `post-stamped` 4 (`EXIT_NOT_STORED`, via `relayExitFor`), `close-cards` 4 (`EXIT_HALF_WRITE`, and the same 4 for an unconfirmed close), `label-write` and `issue-create` 5 (`exitForResult` → `EXIT_PLATFORM_REFUSAL`). UNCONFIRMED is 6 in every tool that takes the relay. The paragraph states the registers as they are on that branch; the rule — read, never retry — is the same in all four.

## Line budget — ceiling 82, headroom 0, paid in place (+9 / −9)

Nine lines are retired. Each is a restatement; the line that keeps the rule is named beside it (line numbers on `main` at 544767d).

| 13 — a rate-limit refusal binds to the refused identity; switching channels is a retry | `platform-readings.md` 122, 125 |
| 14 — the other side is a way out only under a different identity (`GET /user` vs the refused id) | `platform-readings.md` 125 (the `GET /user` test), 96 (one identity inside a seat) |
| 38 — label/assignee writes go through `label-write.mjs` (four steps, read-back) | `SKILL.md` 394; `os-dev.md` 304; the tool's own header |
| 44 — every write carries `Content-Type: application/json`; the 415 and its discriminant | `platform-readings.md` 119–120 |
| 54 — never MCP `update_pull_request`; ready/draft and auto-merge take the ccr routes | `.claude/settings.json` deny list; `SKILL.md` 610; the ccr rows at 48 and 52 of this file |
| 60 — a REST-gated seat falls back to one targeted MCP `search_issues` | `platform-readings.md` 115, 211 |
| 72 — whether auto-merge goes through the queue is answered by trying the action, not a field | `platform-readings.md` 9; rows 73–75 of this file keep the three criteria |

No line was re-wrapped; every line is ≤ 120 bytes (`check:pm-skill-ratchet` green on the head).

## Landing order
